text.p: Italian bond futures held to firmer levels in late afternoon trading supported by the strong lira and rising hopes that the Bank of Italy may cut its key discount rate later this month, dealers said.

The lira pushed ahead early in the day helped by the firmer trend to the dollar, prompting the view that Italy could cut interest rate once December preliminary CPI inflation data is published later this month, they added.
"The lira's strength inevitably brings people to think that a discount rate cut could be just around the corner," said one LIFFE trader in London.

With the December BTP futures contract on LIFFE expiring on Wednesday, operators continue to roll forward contracts to March, but both contracts were helped higher in the optimistic mood on the market, dealers said.

Operators are now watching for Dec preliminary CPI data due mid-month which they hope will show a further fall in inflation after preliminary November data slipped to 2.6 percent from October's 3.0 percent. The official Nov data is due Thursday.
"Italy is showing the way higher today, but bunds and Treasuries are firmer and they will give support if any serious profit-taking sets in," the LIFFE trader said.

Dealers noted that Italy's January-November budget deficit had increased to 135.3 trillion lire so far in 1996, implying that it will top the 130 trillion lire 1996 deficit that government officials had recently forecast.
